player.design_purpose: move_speed_mps sets the pace of positioning against enemies whose speeds are below. melee_reach_m is how far in front of the player a single-target strike connects. cone_degrees is the first-person area-strike arc (D-012): 'area' means the slice of the horde you are facing, which is why training mobs into a bunch pays.

melee.design_purpose: Slower than the player so kiting works, but relentless while you stay near (D-012 training); gives up only when you genuinely leave (give_up_distance_m).

ranged.design_purpose: Keeps its distance and chips with fire so the player learns fire damage exists before the boss; closing on it is the counter.

fast.design_purpose: Outruns the player; packs punish standing still and reward area strikes. The long give_up_distance_m makes hounds the dangerous disengage: escaping them costs distance and risk.

boss.design_purpose: The breath telegraph must be long enough to read and MOVE: the cone is dodged spatially (step or dash out of it), never by invulnerability. Resistance preparation stays mandatory because a horde fight will eventually catch you inside a cone.

skills.design_purpose: Dash is pure movement (D-012): in first person, position is the defence - step or dash out of the breath cone, outpace the train. No invulnerability frames; distance and cooldown live in skills.json.

design_purpose: round_seconds is the bridge between the sim's round-based encounter (the balance oracle) and real time: attack_period_rounds, breath periods and skill cooldowns become seconds by multiplying by it. Everything else here is time-and-space feel that the round model cannot express; damage, life and mitigation never live in this file (ADR-0003).

horde.design_purpose: D-012 stupid-zombie horde feel. Separation makes chasers push apart into a physical train instead of stacking, so bunching them is a skill. give_up_seconds is how long the player must stay beyond a chaser's give_up_distance_m before it loses interest - no eternal aggro, no instant leash.
